standard_prerequisites.name: A morphism of schemes is affine if and only if the inverse image of every affine open of the target is affine
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: This is the criterion applied to g at proof line 1976 and to f at proof lines 1976-1978
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the single condition that has to be checked for the composite, and is applied twice in the counted proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Preimages compose: the inverse image under a composite is the inverse image of the inverse image
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at proof line 1978 to rewrite the preimage under g composed with f
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the open set whose affineness has to be established for the composite.

core_obligations: Let f : X to Y and g : Y to Z be affine morphisms and let U be an affine open subset of Z (proof lines 1975-1976).
Apply affineness of g to get that the inverse image of U in Y is affine, and then affineness of f to get that the inverse image of that affine open in X is affine (proof lines 1976-1978).
Rewrite that set as the inverse image of U under the composite and conclude that the composite is affine, since U was an arbitrary affine open of Z (proof line 1978).
proof_roadmap: Check the defining criterion for the composite at an arbitrary affine open U of the target: the preimage is affine because it is the preimage under f of an affine open produced by g (proof lines 1974-1979).
difficulty_reason: The claim is that for affine morphisms f : X to Y and g : Y to Z the composite g composed with f is affine (statement lines 1969-1972). The proof is a four-line verification of the defining criterion: it takes an arbitrary affine open U of Z, uses affineness of g to make the preimage in Y affine, applies affineness of f to that affine open, and rewrites the result as the preimage under the composite (proof lines 1974-1979). It is H2: the argument is complete and self-contained and the only input is the standard affine criterion, so no H3 claim would be honest here, and the value of the item lies in the faithful short proof rather than in difficulty.
